title: Symbol and BigInt in modern JavaScript
hook: `symbol` creates unique keys that never collide with string properties. `bigint` stores integers larger than `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — essential for IDs, ledgers, and timestamps beyond 2⁵³.

blocks.text: **Symbol** is a primitive type introduced in ES2015. Every `Symbol()` call creates a unique, immutable value — ideal for object property keys that should not clash with user-provided strings. Well-known symbols like `Symbol.iterator` and `Symbol.toStringTag` hook into language protocols. **BigInt** (ES2020) is an arbitrary-precision integer type. Literals end with `n` (`9007199254740991n`). BigInts cannot mix with `number` in arithmetic without explicit conversion — preventing silent precision loss.

entries.plainDefinition: A unique, immutable identifier. `Symbol('desc')` creates a new symbol each time — description is not part of identity.
Built-in symbols on `Symbol` namespace that customize language behavior.
Integer type with no fixed bit width. Use for values beyond ±2⁵³−1 safe integer range.
Largest integer `number` can represent exactly. Beyond this, use `bigint`.

blocks.text: Twitter/X snowflake IDs and blockchain balances exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. Parsing them as `number` silently rounds — use `BigInt`. Symbols prevent library code from overwriting user keys: `const _cache = Symbol('cache')` on a class instance is invisible to `Object.keys()`. In C#, `long` handles 64-bit integers; beyond that you use `BigInteger`. JavaScript splits the problem: `number` for doubles, `bigint` for integers — no `decimal` type.

blocks.title: When to reach for each
blocks.body: Symbol → hidden metadata, protocol hooks (`iterator`, `toStringTag`), enum-like constants without string collision. BigInt → snowflake IDs, crypto amounts, factorials, anything past 9_007_199_254_740_991.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Create a unique Symbol key
items.body: `const key = Symbol('label'); obj[key] = value;` — not enumerable in `for...in` or `Object.keys`.

items.title: Reuse a global Symbol
items.body: `Symbol.for('app.id')` registers in global registry; `Symbol.keyFor(sym)` retrieves the string key.

items.title: Keep number and bigint separate
items.body: `1n + 2` throws TypeError. Use `1n + BigInt(2)` or convert explicitly.

rows: Erased — same as JS at run time

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Parsing snowflake IDs as `number` — silent rounding. Mixing `bigint` and `number` in math. Expecting `JSON.stringify` to handle BigInt. Using `new Symbol()` — Symbol is not a constructor; call `Symbol()` directly. Assuming `Symbol('x') === Symbol('x')` — they are always different unless from `Symbol.for`.

blocks.text: Symbols are opaque property keys — `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` returns them but they skip `JSON.stringify`. Private class fields (`#field`) are a newer alternative for true encapsulation; symbols remain useful for cross-cutting protocols. BigInt uses arbitrary-length two's-complement representation in engines — operations can be slower than `number`. `BigInt.asIntN` / `asUintN` wrap to fixed width for bitwise interop. `typeof 1n` is `'bigint'`. Division on BigInt truncates toward zero (like C# integer division). For money, neither `number` nor `bigint` gives decimal fractions — use a library or integer cents (same advice as C# `decimal` vs `double`).

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: No JSON; no Math.sqrt on bigint

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Saying BigInt works in JSON natively. Claiming two `Symbol('a')` are equal. Mixing bigint and number without mentioning the TypeError.

interviewTakeaways: Every `Symbol()` is unique — description does not affect identity.
Cannot mix bigint and number without explicit conversion; JSON.stringify rejects BigInt.
60s: Symbol for unique keys and protocols. BigInt for large integers. No JSON for BigInt. 2⁵³ safe limit on number.
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'Symbol is like a string enum.' Strong: 'Each Symbol() is unique; use Symbol.for for shared registry.'
Parsing Twitter snowflake IDs as number — silent precision loss.
Strong answer: 'BigInt past 2⁵³. Serialize as string for JSON. Symbols for hidden keys and iterator protocol.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript 3.2+ supports `bigint` literals and `unique symbol` for branded keys. Still no JSON support at run time.
C# `long` is 64-bit fixed. `BigInteger` is arbitrary like JS `bigint`. C# has no Symbol equivalent — use access modifiers.
